descriptions./customer-driven-ai-cti-project/: Run intelligence work as a gated delivery program that connects customer decisions, validated evidence, threat models, telemetry, and production detections.
descriptions./customer-driven-ai-cti-project/docs/: Apply a customer-led, AI-assisted threat intelligence method with requirements, evidence controls, analyst gates, telemetry mapping, and measurable outcomes.
descriptions./customer-driven-ai-cti-project/docs/eco: Navigate the connected 1200km research set and choose the right field manual, actor profiles, workbench, or repository for each stage of CTI delivery.
descriptions./customer-driven-ai-cti-project/docs/fac: Keep three connected CTI books consistent by following clear ownership rules for methodology, delivery gates, actor facts, and production-readiness guidance.
descriptions./customer-driven-ai-cti-project/docs/inf: Find the published Medium series and its visual assets in one source-linked index covering the workflow, execution method, templates, and reference toolkit.
descriptions./customer-driven-ai-cti-project/docs/met: Use one delivery document to move cyber threat intelligence from customer requirements through evidence, telemetry, hunting, detection, validation, and handoff.
Establish the analytic standards, governance, scoring, roles, artifacts, and readiness criteria required for defensible CTI-to-detection delivery.
Execute phases 0–14 with activities, validation tests, templates, evidence gates, and exit criteria for a controlled intelligence-to-detection engagement.
Use AI workflow cards, quality gates, registers, worked examples, and delivery artifacts to start and govern a defensible CTI engagement from week one.
descriptions./customer-driven-ai-cti-project/docs/pra: Practice the method with a synthetic project kit containing fabricated identities, events, decisions, artifacts, and outcomes for safe replay and training.
Trace a synthetic logistics scenario from a CISO decision through PIRs, evidence, telemetry, detection engineering, pilot review, and executive reporting.
Inspect the sample Sigma rule, Sentinel and Splunk queries, unit tests, and validation evidence used to detect privileged identity and backup-deletion activity.
Use a fabricated logistics organization to practice PIR scoping, cloud-identity threat modeling, a 30-day engineering decision, and evidence-led delivery.
Review sample Gate A–F evidence packages showing analyst validation, confidence records, approval state, and a conditional monitor-only production start.
Run the supplied cloud-identity dataset through the replay script and compare the generated JSON result with the expected synthetic detection outcome.
Follow CSV records that connect a customer decision to evidence, intelligence requirements, detection ownership, pilot health, and final acceptance.
View synthetic SVG outputs from the worked case, including the register dashboard, replay result, gate status, and executive summary used in the method.
descriptions./customer-driven-ai-cti-project/docs/pro: Review the documented public release history and the scope of the initial stable documentation package without relying on undocumented product claims.
Check which methodology sections have been retired, what replaces them, and the target removal release; the current public release retires none.
See planned validation, schema, automation, and practitioner-package work while keeping future intentions clearly separated from released capabilities.
Understand the semantic release policy for public methodology and artifact changes, including reproducibility expectations and required release records.
descriptions./customer-driven-ai-cti-project/docs/pub: Open canonical Medium sources for the four-part project series and locate the checked-in local copies that preserve the documentation source material.
descriptions./customer-driven-ai-cti-project/docs/sta: Define the minimum fields for reusable PIR, SIR, EEI, evidence, threat-model, and detection outputs so every handoff remains complete and auditable.
Apply evidence-based ATT&CK technique selection and D3FEND relationships, then connect validated mappings to customer decisions and defensive deliverables.
Interpret MUST, SHOULD, and MAY consistently so requirements remain auditable, exceptions are recorded, and methodology claims retain clear strength.
Validate machine-readable examples, telemetry field mappings, links, and replay outputs with the repository checks required before publishing changes.
descriptions./customer-driven-ai-cti-project/docs/wor: Move from customer decisions to production detections through a 15-phase operating map with explicit evidence, ownership, validation, and acceptance gates.
